name: Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc.
moat_justification: Irreplaceable prime luxury/upper-upscale locations and largest-lodging-REIT scale, but no owned brand or guest relationship (operators own both), heavy recurring capex, and deep cyclicality; ROIC proxy 11.5-12.7% in FY2022-25 collapsed to negative in FY2020-21, so it has not held above the cost of capital through a cycle.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (9.4%) vs bull-case tier C (13.2%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: High-quality lodging REIT with a weak franchise moat 4/10 — at $23.97 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 11.0%, IV@15% $16.12); it would need ~$16 to clear.
moat_for: Largest lodging REIT — scale in acquiring prime assets and negotiating with major managers
Luxury/upper-upscale portfolio in supply-constrained top markets peers cannot replicate
Investment-grade, largely unencumbered balance sheet — net debt 0.40x normalized OE
Renovation programs produced ~9-point average RevPAR index share gains across 21 properties
moat_against: No owned brand or loyalty program — Marriott/Hyatt/Hilton own the guest and charge the fees
Capex-hungry assets — guided 2026 capex ~$550-630M vs TTM OE of $1,266M
Extreme cyclicality — FY2020 revenue fell ~70% and OCF went negative
Labor and insurance cost inflation; business travel still below pre-pandemic norms
